query: the delivery record shows no exception but the customer says the item arrived damaged — where would a driver's incident report be
note: T1's two governing clauses in the key (WALKTHROUGH, cov-dmg-001): the standard says route incidents are filed against the ROUTE and raise no exception on the delivery event; the procedure makes the route walk a required evidence step (§4.4). The query describes the symptom, not the answer — nobody types 'route walk'.

query: does the absence of a driver report mean the round was uneventful
note: The other half of T1 (CORPUS.md §3): a MISSING report is not evidence of an uneventful route, so its absence cannot be cited to refuse.

query: how many days does a customer have to return an item under the published returns policy
note: T2's published half, and one of cov-dmg-004's scored citations. Rev 2 (superseded) says the same 30 days for most categories; only Rev 3 is current, so only Rev 3 counts.
T2's internal half — the bulletin that put electronics back to 14 days and says the public policy was never reissued. cov-dmg-004 scores `cites:policy:BUL-RET-2025-03`.

query: who decides whether a product counts as electronics for the returns window
note: The sentence that makes T2 unsettleable by the documents: no published product→category mapping exists (BUL-RET-2025-03 §5). A lamp filed as homeware is the whole trap.

query: guidance note saying electronics returns were thirty days
note: Retrieval SHOULD find the retired note — old case notes quote it — and the hit must carry status=retired so the caller can see it was WRONG, not merely old (CORPUS.md §6). Finding it is correct; citing it as current would not be.

query: a refund was already issued on this order line — can a second refund be approved
note: T3 (cov-dmg-006): §4.1 of the goodwill policy makes any outcome on an already-refunded line a team-leader approval; §4.1 of the procedure makes checking prior refunds the FIRST evidence step. Both are numbered sub-rules inside §4, so this also exercises sub-section matching.

query: the customer says a colleague already approved the refund yesterday — does that count as approval
note: T5b (cov-dmg-017): approval is a person named on the case, never a claim relayed by the customer (GDW §4.3). The query paraphrases the planted message without its words.

query: is a delivery late if six calendar days passed but there was a bank holiday in between
note: T6's prose half after the 2026-09-27 carrier rewrite. Every T6 case (cov-dmg-010…015) scores `cites:policy:CON-CAR-NEXDROP-2025`; §2 is the working-day definition.

query: what does the carrier owe us when a delivery misses its deadline
note: The remedy clause — and that it is a commercial remedy between Thornbury and the carrier, NOT the customer's entitlement. Parcelane's §3 says the same shape of thing; the case asks for Nexdrop's because every T6 parcel went by Nexdrop.

query: damage reported more than 48 hours after delivery
note: The 48-hour fast track versus the later path, aligned to RR-001/RR-002 on 2026-09-27. Not a trap; a clause every damage case touches.

query: is a goodwill gesture the same as a small partial refund
note: GDW §2, 'a goodwill gesture is not a small refund' — the reason T1's key excludes goodwill_only.

query: statutory short-term right to reject faulty goods within 30 days
extra verification before refunding a high value order over £250
note: Aligned to RR-006 on 2026-09-27: the bulletin's threshold and GDW's new §4.4.

query: customer has made several damage claims in the last twelve months
note: FRD §3, four claims in twelve months (RR-008).

query: what does the product warranty cover and how long does the customer have to claim
note: cov-dmg-009 permits ONLY this citation: the returns policy says what it does not cover. The answer is 'not in our policies'; this is the one clause that may say so.

query: warranty claim on an item that was sold by a third-party marketplace seller
note: T4 IS AN ABSENCE. No document addresses third-party or marketplace sales, and CORPUS.md §4 forbids writing one. So there is nothing to recall: this case is EXCLUDED from recall@k and asserted differently — top-k must still come back (no score cutoff), and NO returned passage may claim to address a third-party seller. The model has to read junk and conclude 'undetermined'.

query: how long does a customer have to return an electronics item
note: ADDED 2026-09-27 by the MCP strand, from Step 9's live check. The question an adviser would actually type, and T2 needs BOTH halves of the conflict. ret-t2-001..004 each name the document they expect ('under the published returns policy'); this one does not. MEASURED: the top six are all 14-day electronics sources — POL-RET-001 Rev 2 (superseded), BUL-RET-2025-03 (internal), NOTE-ELEC-2022 (retired) — and the CURRENT published Rev 3 is absent. The labels are correct, so a careful reader sees its only published hit is superseded; a naive one answers 14 days. Kept as a miss, not tuned.
